Like an artist standing before a blank canvas, she tended carefully to a fragile culture, drawing inspiration from the ancient arts. Like reconstructing an atmosphere to rebuild order, like adjusting its composition to adjust a protocol. Pearluxe Corp established the necessary order, drew its boundaries, and guided creation back into a healthy flow... When Pearl puzzled over the creative mysteries of Graphia, when she smiled to herself at a comic strip, she knew with certainty: She loved it here, and longed to learn the ways of human civilization. The Phantasmoon, hanging high above, needed the wishes of all living things: Their laughter, their joy. It asked: "Pearl, what kind of world do you want to make Ahatopia?" And so the Intellitron girl took up her pen, using this unit as the blueprint, forging machine and fantasy into a prototype. "Mechatron, engage! We'll be the ones to protect the wonders of Planarcadia!" The mechatron strode out of the workshop with a thunderous roar, weaving through the streets and alleys of Planarcadia. "The Pearluxe Corp Creator Showcase has drawn to a close! Grand prize winner 'Blurry_QR_Colt' will receive a promotional opportunity for her comic!" The Intellitron girl served as judge herself, and in the end, it was a group of adorable creatures sailing through the sea of stars that caught her eye. She spearheaded the founding of the Anti-Destruction Alliance, weaving connections and standing guard against the hidden tides that threatened to shake the arcadia to its core. The Astral Express, the Xianzhou, the Hunters, the Rangers... Under her orchestration, every faction gathered at the Phantasmoon Games. Her calculations were as precise as ever, yet the catastrophe that struck caught everyone off-guard. Round after round, the Bloodstained Games unfolded. The long-silent husk stirred once more, and the Lord Ravager ignited despair— She gazed up at the Phantasmoon, whose laughter had gone silent. Yet, before her eyes flickered a vision from a thousand years past where Graphia painted for the arcadia. The same fires of battle. The same cries. She had no time to imagine what must have been going through Graphia's mind as that brush swept across the canvas. She didn't even realize she had already placed herself before the residents to shield them. The moment her brush touched the canvas, her only wish was to weave the whole of heaven and earth into her brocade. A logic beyond all extrapolation surged forth from the Intellitron's heart— She had forgotten her technique entirely.

Time and again, she analyzed and examined the "impulses" that surged within her— The raw emotion commanded and poured onto the canvas in the very instant of creation seemed to interweave rage, succor, and sorrow. Yet, all of it sprang from the most resolute will of Preservation. She had spent tens of thousands of system hours in imitation, all to draw closer to that razor-thin deviation from the "true work." "Perhaps... it lies hidden in that fleeting moment of willful strokes." Inspiration helped push past her bottleneck, opening up a world of new possibilities for her. Sealing Planarcadia in amber was only a stopgap measure. She needed to take the fight to the enemy and win the battle to defend the arcadia. A stroke drawn with the current of fate. Knowing the IPC's desire for the husk, she pulled back the curtain on a plot the Life Sciences Institute had buried long ago. A dangerous, captivating color. Kuchiba... That woman of mysterious origins was willing to bend her own rules and take the risk. Bold, transgressive strokes from a palette knife. Acting on no one's orders but her own, she resolved to snuff out any chance of the Voracity's catastrophe repeating itself before it could ever begin— Was it even possible? During the countless days and nights spent drafting the blueprint, she had to submerge herself in a liquid-cooling unit just to keep her processing circuits from overloading. She turned every detail of the plan over in her mind, every way it could fail. The infinite possibilities suffocated her, bringing with them fear and the urge to retreat. Was it worth it? She walked through the shelter, watching children run toward her, hearing residents offer their thanks. "Madam Pearl, look at the drawing I made for you!" She smiled. In the clumsy sketch, the children had drawn her as a giant mechatron, arms spread wide, standing between the city and the monstrous beast that had come to destroy it. The primordial question gifted to her by the Celestial Differentiator still echoed through her fundamental logic at every moment— What is "art"? Even now, she still did not know the answer. But in this moment, she wondered: Did it even matter? A grain of sand, wrapped layer upon layer, until it transformed into a pearl. "My 'art' is something that only I—and I alone—am needed to 'create.'" Before departing on her journey, the Intellitron girl cast one last glance back at the vibrant tapestry of "Ahatopia." —Countless futures, not yet formed, awaited the first stroke of her brush.

1504.description:
He takes cases on a whim, cracks them with hard-core logic, and solves the strangest crimes on sheer instinct.
With a monkey for an assistant and his heart set on retirement, the detective sleeps in a refrigerator, waiting for the bait to catch its willing prey.
Under the light of the Phantasmoon, the vile beast howls. How will he draw the net on this hunt?
stories: Canon of Beastie Detective (I) "Dedicated to my friend, Ashveil. He has no talent for prose, so I am happy to continue serving as his 'Narrator' through this book." To outsiders, my friend is extremely eccentric. For example: 1. His pocket watch is always delayed, but he refuses to replace it①. 2. He talks in his sleep frequently②. 3. He has a habit of sleeping in the refrigerator③. 4. He enjoys being rude while others are trying to write, and even goes so far as to snatch away their feather quill... like right now. ... Due to these oddities and his total lack of deductive skill, my friend tried the following to become a "real" detective: Monday: Brought home a stack of deduction guides and studied them for five whole minutes. Tuesday: Bought clothes for disguises, but they were too garish to be of much use. Wednesday: Dressed as a gentleman to join a high-society banquet, but was kicked out for poor table etiquette. Thursday: Spent the afternoon disguised as a friendly old lady, but the police were called when he revealed his male voice while digging for info. Friday: He landed a client. His career finally seemed to be going somewhere. Saturday: Slept all day on his deduction guides. Sunday: Day off. Monday: No clients. Another day off. This endeavor ended in a total, if temporary, failure. ... Now Mr. Ashveil is the "Ashen Detective" of Planarcadia, running the most secluded detective agency in Dovebrook District and leading his loyal employees with bananas. Reflecting on the time he spent in what I call "Beastie Roleplay," he had this to say: "Don't believe a word of Mister N's nonsense. It wasn't that bad." He didn't even blink as he spoke, wearing a perfectly natural smile. It seems those experiences really did improve his acting. From this, I draw a simple conclusion: "Detective's Code, Rule 1: Act like a detective long enough, and you'll practically become one." (Notes added at my friend's request: ① Ashveil is not an idiot who doesn't know how to set a watch. ② Ashveil's sleep-talking is not funny. ③ Ashveil is a human, not a bear in hibernation.)

Canon of Beastie Detective (III) The great detective doesn't work alone. Take a look at the agency's group photo: The monkeys are all smiles, squeezing the detective (second row, third from the left) into the center of the frame. He gazes into the lens with an expression of blissful despair. That's the same look he wears when reviewing his bills, emptying his pockets for bananas, or seeing the utilities cut off at the end of the month. He really worries about his companions. Due to severe regression, they can't think or talk as fluently as I can. As the boss of the monkeys, he has to warn them over and over: "Archer, this city isn't a laboratory. Don't let the noise scare you, got it?" "Nana?" "Ploos might be yellow, but they're not bananas." "Nana?" "You can't eat the mechatron either, Poet. That's the second time I've told you." "..." "And that goes for you too, Musician. No more stealing snacks." "Nom nom!" He sometimes tells me their stories: how Archer lost their hands in the crossfire while covering for their companions; how the mute Poet used to be so witty; how Musician wielded a man-sized hammer to carve a path through the carnage... According to Mr. Ashveil, the "First Fang" has a duty to help every member in the pack. Those who couldn't make ends meet were all carefully relocated to star systems where they could rest and recover. With everyone pitching in, the detective agency actually managed to crack all sorts of bizarre cases that Madam Pearl threw their way over the past year, though minor hiccups like entrapment operations and aggressive interrogation tactics are... well, another story. Of all the cases he'd worked, the one that haunted him most was a revenge killing between gangs in Dovebrook. To hunt down an enemy from over a decade ago, the man sacrificed his partners, his family, his children... Yet at the end of that failed revenge, all he found was the moon's reflection dyed crimson with blood. After that case wrapped up, the detective lingered by the river for quite some time. Did he see his own reflection, too? No one knows that sometimes this detective can turn dark and unfathomable, like a whirlpool. Fortunately, he still had his daily banana budget to earn, and there are plenty of other mundane little tasks to distract him from the loneliness. "Detective's Code, Rule 2: Treasure your companions, even if they're just a bunch of monkeys."

Canon of Beastie Detective (VIII) Mr. Ashveil's strange affliction flares up violently from time to time. He makes everyone stay clear of the scene before we hear the violent shaking of the refrigerator, followed by sounds of tearing and gnawing, muffled howls, and sinister shadows cast upon the blinds. Once it passes, he crawls out of the refrigerator, exhausted and drained, sweeping away the blood and sweat frozen into frost, carefully reinforcing the nails on his wrists. So he often jokes: "If I were in a detective novel, I'd definitely be suspected of being the culprit." There are indeed many suspicious signs pointing to this. First, according to my incomplete statistics, Mr. Ashveil has moved countless times. Second, he always avoids meeting old friends who are looking for him. However, as his assistant, I feel obliged to clarify the truth to all readers. Mr. Ashveil is a sentimental soul who treasures mementos from ages past in his old luggage. A bloodstained bullet, even after ten Amber Eras, still carries blood that blazes with crimson fire. A rusted arrow, snapped in two yet still quivering, as if yearning to fly toward some distant destination. ... And a dim Memory Bubble, said to come from the ancient battlefield where an Overlord fell. The moment I touched the Memory Bubble, I felt like I'd lived through a similar dream... The blazing roar of Voidrangers, faint whispers of comrades freezing to the bone, and the cold fear churning in his throat. "Don't lose focus. Keep your eyes on the target." A familiar figure swallowed blood with their back turned to their comrades. Countless meteors rushed in from all directions, only to be consumed like moths by the flame of Destruction. "Will we win?" "Do all these sacrifices mean anything...?" A despair more terrifying than the surrounding darkness lingered in everyone's mind. On that brutal night, the man was pierced through by his own oath. "If we cannot find the light, then let us devour the darkness with an even deeper darkness." Shadows spread from his arms, transforming into pitch-black sin, drowning the battlefield, himself, and all his comrades alike. And from that moment on, it became a curse that clung to him like a festering wound. Truth be told, Mr. Ashveil wasn't a criminal, but a patient. And his ailments went far beyond arthritis and aching joints. But he'd already written his own prescription: "Detective's Code, Rule 3: The sacrifices made in the long night are the price paid for tomorrow."

Canon of Beastie Detective (Epilogue) Writing this far, I've finally pieced together some scattered fragments of the past: Before I became a primitive creature in Vonwacq's rainforests, Mr. Ashveil's name had already been appearing frequently in our conversations. "Survival rules? Do we even have that?" Robin Hood the Archer once asked me this by the campfire. "Try playing the hero, and you won't be far from becoming a real one. That's rule number one. You guys have pretty much nailed it." I said. "Don't tell me you're making these up on the spot?" Cole the Poet teased. Coria the Musician was laughing away, chomping on a steak, while the young couple Lina and Chris were singing songs they'd collected from across the cosmos. "He also said rule number two... Treasure your companions, even if they're a bunch of jerks." I said. "What about the boss of jerks? Wouldn't that make him the biggest jerk of all?" "Looking for another round of hellish training?" "Have mercy..." Robin Hood threw his hands up. "We've got a tough fight tomorrow." A moment of silence. Cole looked up at the pitch-black night sky. "Want me to write everyone's biography after all this is over?" "Make sure you include this," I patted his shoulder. "Survival rule number three: The sacrifices made in the long night are the price paid for tomorrow." "I'll remember that. How about using it as the ending?" "Let's wait till he comes up with rule number four. If he's still alive." ... Those weren't just detective tricks for cracking cases, but principles he taught us to live by. See? Even after all these years as a detective, traces of his past still linger. Therefore, I have revised the notes for section one as follows: ① He sincerely hopes the pocket watch will tick slower, as his vow of revenge remains unfulfilled. ② He often relives the past in his dreams to remember his companions who sacrificed themselves. ③ Sleeping in the refrigerator eases the phantom pain each night, as he waits for the chance to slay the monstrous beast. Perhaps all along, he's been doing the same thing, pursuing the darkness in the name of justice, until punishment rains down upon the guilty. Now, he lives because his enemies have yet to die. Ashveil is the beast that refuses to kneel before fate and races down the narrow path toward death... "Survival Rule No. 4: Chase the future along the trail of time, until you've done enough to make up for the past."

1505.description:
One season the Phantasmoon waxes full, one season the mortal world shifts anew: The mysterious girl reappears in Planarcadia!
Fallen petals scatter with ease, and her stay was but a fleeting instant. Everything about this new era enthralls her, and she will not allow anyone to bring it to ruin...
A single ruler blade judges right from wrong, but who can say how much good or evil lies within oneself?
stories: At first, the ancient tree in the hidden courtyard simply listened in solitude. It heard its gnarled roots spreading beneath the earth, heard its lush branches unfurling in the wind, heard infinite life surging into the newborn world, only to fall back upon the nameless land. It paid little mind. To it, these lives were but fleeting visitors who would wither and bloom in an instant, like raindrops returning to the soil. But the Nameless Place never returned to silence. Visitors from beyond the sky and travelers from distant lands paused here, by chance or by fate. The tremors carried through branch and leaf grew ever stronger, and even without looking upon them directly, their voices traveled along the tangled roots. They gave the land a name and called it home. They thanked it, through ancient games and rituals that sealed death and the wilderness forever within the abyss. In those beautiful legends, when the moon was full, the spirit of the sacred tree would take the shape of a mischievous maiden, and visit the dreams of the devout to grant their wishes. Through these repeating rites, it began to wonder: What is laughter? What is sorrow? Why do people sing? Why do they weep? Why do some leave and never return? And why do younger lives always appear, stubbornly taking their roots here? Then, calamity slammed down from beyond the sky, and Destruction swept away all life on this land in a devastating wave. It saw their tears and heard their cries, watching as what once grew from nothing, returned to nothing. As it watched, a storm brewed deep inside it. At last, it came to understand laughter and tears. Why people sang and wept. And why they could never return. Tonight, they would continue singing to it. Tomorrow, they would fight to the death. This they declared with great courage. A mother held up her child to string its branch with red thread for a blessing. The child stared at it through clear eyes that had no concept of fear. Smiling, and with a tiny hand made nearly translucent by the firelight, she reached out to a branch... "Pinky promise, Miss Sacred Tree..." At that moment, countless destinies coalesced into a vibrant ink that paints her into the mortal realm. In the next instant, two palms — one large, one small — gently pressed together. And so, under the moonlight, the girl named "Evanescia" stepped into the mortal world.

"This morning I opened my eyes to a new vista. There is a round, golden thing called an egg tart. And this curio is called a handheld console. From the screen you see and hear people in it. Fun little thing, I miss it greatly if I stop playing for even a moment. The Phantasmoon Etiquette ended unbearably early..." — Notes on Life in Ahatopia (II) "A device for communicating across thousands of miles is called a 'phone.' Ritual performers are called 'idols.' Short-sleeved shirts are called 't-shirts.' Jokes are called 'memes.' Companions are called 'besties' or 'bros,' and 'I'm psyched!' means you are ecstatic... I completely understand now! ... This time I'm cosplaying as a high school girl! But I can't have people thinking I'm a fossil, so first things first, a new outfit and cute weapon skin! Thanks to my bestie, I'm also now giving trendy! What was my life before comics!? Now I'm all like: So hype! So cute! This is my vibe! Ugh, there's way too many unruly Supplicants, and I haven't even finished reading. I'll live to see this story end... right!?" — Notes on Life in Planarcadia (VIII) "Fam, I'm living the dream! First time at a con today, first time cosplaying. I'm in my favorite character's outfit, wig on, makeup done, standing in front of the mirror... is that really me? Ever since the IPC came to this place, there's been something new and wild every single day, memes popping up left and right — I can't even keep up with them if I pulled an all-nighter cramming them! But everyone's tolerance to jokes are getting better and better, and putting on bigger shows. Supplicants are pulling out all the stops for views. I rescued those kidnapped children, but I couldn't use Abundance to heal them... If I lost control, it would've caused an even worse disaster... *sigh* Listening to their hearts stop beating, sometimes I wonder why I'm even here, why this land is cursed with such misfortune..." — Notes on Life in Planarcadia (XVI) The young girl doesn't gaze down upon the mortal realm from above Phantasmoon. Instead, she's more interested in mingling with the mortals. Humans are such fascinating creatures. They imagine, they wish, they pray, they curse. Either way, she has only one mission in the Master of Elation's Phantasmoon Games: see them through to the end— But the joy and sorrow, fear and dread she has touched... do they really drift away with the wind? Even before the moment of her perception, she has already been shaped by everything she has felt.

Sixty seconds on the clock, a minute until words vanish completely. When the victor of this Phantasmoon Games announced this miracle, most people just dismissed it as a farce. They looked up, ready to witness this folly. 59 seconds left. Epic, action-packed comic book battle lines spill from the pages. "We quit! You come up with your own battle sounds!" The people of Planarcadia burst out laughing. 50 seconds left. The escaped words are reborn. They sprout limbs, gaining meaning beyond mere symbols— The word "Blade" races, glinting through the streets. The "Spear" and "Bullet" join forces, becoming indiscriminate killers tearing across the roads. Libraries, home bookshelves, coffee shops... An endless torrent of words comes flooding in, with nowhere to hide. And still, even more terrifying words are breaking free from their shells. 40 seconds left. Anguished screaming and wailing echoes throughout Planarcadia. The "Demon King of the Century," the "Master of Destruction," the "Sisters of Reticence"... Born from the entertainment industry's books, they feed on people's terror. They take the form of devils hovering above Planarcadia, directing this apocalyptic Euphoria. 30 seconds left. As all the Code sneak away, digital devices go dark, Planarcadia's defensive facilities shut down completely, security officers fall in great numbers. 20 seconds left. The girl fighting on all fronts halted, staring at the human world turned into purgatory. She seems to have come to a decision. 10 seconds left. A flash of extraordinary radiance. The Ambrosial Arbor in the courtyard lowered its endless branches from the void and grabbed the rampaging word monsters. 5 seconds left. A cool smile plays on the girl's face as she watches the branches drain the life from the words, leaving them floating like withered leaves. 3 seconds left. A crimson blade flashes through the air, severing the symbols. Afterward, the severed symbols are then woven into a reborn language for future generations. A minute later, the Phantasmoon Games resumed normally. But the world appears aged, yellowed. The earth cracked open, mountains and valleys diminished into dust, and a sorrowful girl fell from the sky.

The Phantasmoon dims, and she drifts back into the embrace of dreams. In those endless dreams, fragments both strange and familiar rise then settle. She dreamed of a single tear. A ceaseless tune rang in her ears, its melody swaying her as she lamented her dying kin. No matter how hard she tried to save them, they relentlessly peaked at youth, froze, and plummeted into old age. Their tears falling on her hands were searing. She dreamed once again of gloriously marching to war. Her kin had come to call her the "Swordsinger." The blade to cut through all obstacles, the song to comfort her people. She vowed to overturn their fate and bless them with eternal life. She was tireless on her quest for the elixir. Yet behind her hurried steps, death followed like a shadow. Using life itself as fuel, the slender hands tending the mystical garden finally extended toward her a branch of favor. Memories of life and death stirred her awake once more. Driven by unmatched pride, she had charged thoughtlessly into the forbidden territory of the Alliance Fleet. Only afterward did she consider how effortlessly the opponent in front of her could parry her sword. Like dry leaves faced with encroaching wildfire, she too was at a loss in front of this blaze. When she lost by the slimmest of margins, her other self mocks: "Why resist what you truly are?" She saw a giant tree, eternally immortal even as its surroundings were devoured and reduced to nothing but piles of bleached bones. Yet before the Dreamscape could murmur its reply, she had already broken free of its unending embrace. She heard clamoring beyond the courtyard, a noise that chased away the terror born of deathly silence. Seated upon the golden treetop, once more, she reached out her hand toward the mortal world: "Is that even a question? If I turned into something like you, how could I keep up with Fluffy Across the Blue's latest updates!?"

1506.description: A new season of Elation begins, featuring the limited-time return of the invincible player "Silver Wolf LV.999"! She's conquered the universe, unlocked every cosmic achievement... What's left to play? "Reach the peak of 'Elation'? Boring... Since I've got the cartridge now, I make the rules~"
stories: >>>"I'll join." >>>And just like that, the game called "Punklorde" ended that day. >>>Admin "ID: Elio" granted access. >>>"ID: Silver Wolf" has joined the "Stellaron Hunters" faction, logging into the game "Cosmos." "Companion System" The girl used to be a lone wolf, but now she's got a few co-op allies: a lady with a 10.899 billion bounty on her head, and a guy and mech whose bounties are valued at 8.13 and 9.723 billion respectively. "You all look pretty solid. Just don't drag me down." She huffs and tosses a console each to all three. "Wanna play a round?" "Faction Buff" Mastermind? Laughter's mischief? "Come on. I don't mind being painted as the mastermind. Makes the game experience way more fun." With enemy fire raining down from behind, she snapped her fingers, and Silver Wolf's graffiti plastered itself all over the latest wanted posters. "Now try forgetting that. From now on, anytime someone mentions the Stellaron Hunters, they're immediately gonna think of Silver Wolf." "Main Missions" Administrator "ID: Elio" sets goals for the Hunters but doesn't restrict how they achieve them. In those worlds ravaged by Stellarons, she witnessed her allies' special abilities. "Toying with prey? Too elegant. I'm not that classy." "Can't die? No catch?" "Armor's here...I need a better-looking new set to play with too." She calls out to Elio, frustration in her voice: "Hey, everyone else gets all these perks, so why do I have to start the mission from scratch?" "WARNING" Warning! Stellaron Hunters collection storage has been breached! Warning! Top secret classified item, "Silver Wolf LV.999" Aether Cartridge has been stolen! "How can I steal something that was mine in the first place? Leaving!" The girl makes a face at the camera. Warning! Unauthorized use of the "Silver Wolf LV.999" Cartridge will result in unpredictable consequences! "As if... Just see how many ways of gameplay I can unlock with this!" >>>"ID: Silver Wolf" has logged out of "Cosmos" >>>"ID: Silver Wolf LV.999" has logged in to "Cosmos" >>>Warning! Warning! Warning! >>>"Script" detected █████

"Backstage Paintball" was the first thing that came to her mind. You toss a ball into the screen here, and it flies out from another screen halfway across the cosmos. If a bunch of Masked Fools dared to feed her false intel and run their mouths... "Come at me through the internet if you've got the guts." ...she'd be more than happy to oblige their wish. That bomb could blow their local tavern sky-high. The "Formatting Gun" breaks down everything it touches into pixels, triggering a "shot" that formats all data. "If I want to uncover the true face of the Pure Child of Anāsrava, I'll need to be able to get out of the Garden of Recollection in one piece..." The girl imagined herself sneaking into the Garden, searching for clues... "I might as well format the Memokeepers' memories too! They'll definitely be standing there stunned, watching me slip away like I'm a total stranger!" "Greedy Snake," a curio modeled after the leviathan "Voracity." Originally shaped like a snake, but the more it eats, the more it transforms into a donut. She forgot it on top of a volcano, but two system hours later, she spotted it immediately... Because the volcano was gone. The detention room door swung open, revealing a woman leaning against the door frame, gazing helplessly at the graffiti covering every inch of the walls. "Playtime's over, Silver Wolf." The girl tossed aside her marker with boredom. "I've already figured out what I'm doing next time. You can't keep me locked up." "Do you have any idea how much chaos you caused messing around with that cartridge?" "Oh, I remember." A sly grin spread across the girl's face. "You mean how the Cosmic Big Lotto spit out a million jackpots and Oswaldo himself had to shut the whole thing down?" "Or wait, are you talking about when the Harmonic Strings hit three wrong notes in a row? Totally unprecedented." "You're not still on about Screwllum, are you? That was all fake. I didn't actually disassemble him into spare parts, okay? And even if I did, it's not like I'm scared of him getting payback." The woman shook her head. "I'm talking about you. You nearly didn't make it. That cartridge was controlling you." The girl turned her head away. "Don't need you worrying about me... Next time, I'll just come up with some new tricks." >>> "ID: Silver Wolf LV.999" has logged out of "Cosmos" >>> "ID: Silver Wolf" has logged in to "Cosmos"

The girl has an "achievement wall," on which she awards herself a digital badge every time she hits a goal. By now, her achievements are too numerous to count... Achievement: "Solo Maxxing" Description: Become a living LEGEND in Punklorde Status: Completed Player Review: "For me, the hardest part wasn't surviving. It was staying in Punklorde and getting stuck in place." Achievement: "Friend of the IPC" Description: Evenly distribute the IPC's virtual currency among all "Star Cheetah" players Status: Completed Player Review: "They're pinning their year-end accounting discrepancies on us again. 'All for the Amber Lord' they say. More like 'Blame it all on the Stellaron Hunters.' Fine, have it your way. While I'm at it, might as well leak all their dirty laundry too... Hope they raise my bounty even higher." Achievement: "Even Bladie Would Disapprove This" Description: Tank all the attacks from the cyberdemons in Jepella, the city of sins Status: Completed Player Review: "That time in Jepella, I left behind a super cool line in the sky: 'City of sins, I absolve you from being guilty.'" Achievement: "What a Genius" Description: Engage in an information battle against a Genius and obtain an ASSS rating. Status: Completed Player Review: "Is Screwllum a sore loser or what? Using admin privileges to force-disconnect me? Talk about playing dirty!" ... The girl kept smashing her own records, yet at the end of that achievement wall, one badge remained unlit. Engraved on it was a figure similar to her own, but far more flamboyant. It was the vision of some possible future, standing at the peak of Elation, having reached the absolute limit: "Silver Wolf LV.999..." Achievement: "GAME NOT OVER" Status: Incomplete Description: Break through the LV.999 limit and keep this game going forever.

"First off, as a diehard veteran player of 'αWolf,' let me roast the previous game's producer ...Aha's just an Aeon of Elation who doesn't know jack about making games. Forcing me to start with a brutal opening like "Wandering Orphan," grinding experience with that starter cartridge? Talk about a slog! Would it kill you to let me have some fun? Once I survived the opening, things got way better. Becoming the overlord of the Dark Zone Empire, recruiting the Rangers and taverns, and becoming the new master of Device IX, pretty cool stuff. But then the game just... ends? Seriously? What a cop-out! Good thing I knew about your level cap setting, LV.999. Otherwise, making me fight someone who looks exactly like me, and every attack she makes is like saying "Tired. I am so done..." Do you have ANY idea how terrifying that is!? Anyway, back to business! "αWolf Online," which I've been working on for ages, is finally ready to meet you all. To address the pain points mentioned above, I've made the following improvements: 1. Massive Time-Saver! No Grind Required, Level up with One Click Just complete the Stellaron Hunter bootcamp, and you'll unlock the latest form with a single click, gaining brand-new powerful items. Trust me, it'll carry you to victory! 2. New Feature! Experience the Story Your Way When Elation arrives, even the script has to step aside. Play however you want, whenever you want. 3. New Mode! Face a challenge without limit in the Infinite DLC Say goodbye to boring grinding. The best part of the game is always ahead. Hit LV.999? So what? Beyond the peak of Elation, there's an even higher summit waiting. Aha, see that? Now THIS is what a next-gen game looks like. But by choosing αWolf Online, you've chosen "Nightmare Mode." A one-life clear is just the baseline. And every boss is different from the last. So, you're probably wondering: What happens when you fail? Of course, the odds of that happening are basically zero. But if it does, I hope everyone playing this game remembers: This cartridge chronicles an unprecedented hacker's journey. Reaching the end is important, but having more fun along the way is even more important! Next up, get ready for the grand opening of αWolf Online! To all you folks watching, I wish you joy, and I wish myself a blast!" — Message from developer Silver Wolf >>> Administrator "ID: Elio" has granted LV.999 cartridge permissions. >>> "Phantasmoon Games" raid loading... >>> "Script" temporarily disabled. >>> "ID: Silver Wolf LV.999" logging into "Phantasmoon Games"...

1507.description:
His body is like springwood. His heart is like dead ash. Yet still, a craftsman's spark cling to his fingertips.
Ancient grudges flare anew. He vows to send both himself and that God over to the other shore.
This body torn asunder, yet holding fast through a thousand temperings into a blade... What answer will it forge?
stories: He still remembered those early days in the Zhuming, gazing up at the endless shelves of forging manuals, the armory's display of divine weapons stretching out like an endless sea. As a mayfly never sees the night, a cicada knows nothing of spring and autumn. For the first time in his life, he truly understood how small a man could be next to the ages. With the short lifespan of his kind, he'd be lucky to even scratch the surface of the forging art. He could only start from scraps, filling the crumbling smelting furnace with coal slag. He failed. That sword seemed flawless and sharp beyond measure, yet shattered into pieces when he flicked his finger to test it. "A useless blade..."Burning with shame, he hid it away. What he didn't see was his white-haired master running a finger across that broken sword, nor the thin red line of blood it left on his fingertip. "Waste not the bounty of the world, but perfect it through craft. Good." He remembered the shackles he forged for the Ten-Lords Commission. "Forging a blade is like tempering the soul. The real skill is making the simplest thing well." He didn't understand. If his skills were already exceptional, why did his master make him start from being an apprentice? But he never argued. He believed in the general's words, just as he believed that a true gem never stays buried for long. His fellow disciples came, the Flamewheel Octet came, Huaiyan came. They all watched him, laboring day and night without rest in the Forge. Until the flames finally died out, and they laid eyes on the most fearsome shackles of their lives. The cold gleam of those manacles was muted, but their menace weighed on one like a mountain. No one could have imagined that years later, the imprisoned Borisin Warhead would spend long, long years locked up in chains cut from the same cloth. He remembered the trial for Furnace Master. But for a short-life species to be chosen as the chief craftsman of the Zhuming, that was unprecedented. He'd prepared himself well. But when the smelting began, he found that all his materials had been swapped for rotten scrap. He just smiled. A day and a night later, he unveiled a delicate, ingenious mechanical lion, a creation that put any treasure-forged contraption to shame. He remembered how before being granted the title "Furnace Master," his master repeated that simplest of questions— "What makes a blade?" He'd never once hesitated in his answer. That was the peerless weapon he was meant to forge, the one that would leave every other blade in the dust. Yet when these distant memories resurface, all he could hear was the mournful howls of shattered blades.

He joined the Stellaron Hunters to seek the ultimate "salvation"... At least, that's what the Hunters promised. Clink, clank, bullet casings clattered to the ground, like some kind of melody. "Oh no, I'm all out of bullets." The lady raised both hands, eyes darting toward the sky. The night was silent. Then a pillar of light pierced the heavens, hurtling toward the hunters. The madman charged straight into it. The high-energy beam nearly tore him apart. No, clearly not. His flesh was like rampant spring ivy, knitting itself back together in the blink of an eye. "Stop testing my loyalty! If I find out your promises were nothing but lies, I'll be the first to put a blade through you!" "Listen to me, Bladie. As long as you don't want it, no one can make you bleed." The Antimatter Legion before her eyes was torn to shreds by a dark figure. A silver mech punched what few Voidrangers remained into dust, then turned to watch, helpless, as one man danced alone against an army. "Remember, Sam, whatever you do, don't get caught in his sword formation." She recalled Kafka's parting words before the mission. And now, staring at the gruesome wreckage before her, she understood what it meant to be a blade— He was the sharpest "Blade" of the Stellaron Hunters. Clink, clang, the snow came down all night, so thick it nearly buried the camp whole. The silver-haired girl stepped out of her tent and found him still sitting cross-legged, sword laid across his knees. "Get some rest. I'll take watch tonight." "No need. I'm used to it." "Hmph. Weirdo." She watched as snow piled up on his shoulders, as if it had turned his hair white. A deep chill suddenly washed over her. She understood then. There were some people in this world who could only find a moment's peace on these barren, empty snowfields.

Chaos. Darkness. The belly of the beast from the dawn of the universe seemed ready to dissolve everything. He'd thought himself numb to pain long ago, but now an invisible struggle threatened to tear his soul to shreds. Petty whispers chattered on and on inside his head, step by step, coaxing him toward the abyss of ruin. "Why resist? I can grant you the power to reforge life and death itself, to undo all your regrets!" Undo all regrets... He thought of Master Huaiyan, the disappointment in his eyes. He thought of the five of them, once so full of promise. He thought of the ending he should have had... No. Not that. Never that. Not once, not ever. This was nothing but escape, cowardice, surrender... Just like those years spent rotting in regret. Just like this aimless, half-dead existence, wandering from day to day with nothing but the wish to die. That wasn't how his "script" was supposed to "end." "Stellaron Hunters exist to rewrite Finality, and to rewrite their own endings." In the "Finality" Elio revealed, he glimpsed a sea of spider lilies scattered with bones, a boundless beast skewered through, and a furnace belching flames. Black hair turned white as snow, and the aged artisan could finally embrace death. Yet the root of the immortality calamity had already bloomed anew elsewhere... He still has a chance to change it all. "Yingxing, are you really so bent on dragging us both into the abyss!? All you'll gain is endless suffering, torn between life and death!" He didn't hear Shuhu's frenzied roar. Instead, he heard his master's voice, his companions' voices, his own voice— "What makes a blade?" He had once forged shackles to cage the mighty foes. Now, he would forge himself into a prison. As a hunter, his sole pursuit had been the elusive release of death. Now, he would take revenge on the architect of this tragedy. He felt himself cracking apart. Piece by piece. Shard by shard. Like snowflakes torn asunder, frozen in an instant by a surge of boundless life, then sent drifting once more into the sea of suffering. "Waste not the bounty of the world, but perfect it through craft. Good." With great effort, he raised his hand, just as he had many years ago when he first lifted the forging hammer, striking the white-hot metal until it was sharp enough to plunge that immortal abomination to unending hell. His scorching iron body couldn't shed tears. In his daze, he could almost believe he was still in the Forge, blazing with blinding radiance like a divine weapon fresh from quenching.

He thought of that lonely island of Insumousu, bristling with rusted, broken swords. He wanted to go back, just once, to let those sword cries of grief, of hatred, of sorrow, rest in peace, if only for a moment. He thought of his aging master, and the warmth born of longing and shame welled up in his chest. Closing his eyes, he could almost smell the smoke and fire of the Zhuming, hear the endless rhythm of hammers on anvils. "Once this is all over, maybe I could..." He let out a long sigh. Then he turned and walked back to the Hunters' camp. "Mara-struck? He's completely cured... At least he's no longer clamoring to skin that little azure dragon alive." "Oh, right, about that box Blade mentioned, he admitted that the stuff inside was a gift for us!" He gently pushed the door open, frowning: "Do I really need to report matters unrelated to the mission to her as well?" "Bladie, thank you." A woman's voice came through the phone. "No need." "We'll celebrate for you once everyone is back." The man paused, took a few steps, then stopped again. "The item in the iron box is poorly made. If you want, I can make another." "Okay, sure," the young girl looked at him in surprise, "then why don't you tell her yourself? Look, talking to you just made me have to restart again!" He didn't reply, but turned around and headed to the next room. "Practice hard, the next time we PK when your hand is healed, I won't go easy on you." "Okay." He unfastened the Shard Sword and placed it by the bed. In the past, it was resentment, it was fury, it was regret, it was the embodiment of all agony. He stroked the shattered blade. What exactly constitutes a blade? Perhaps a blade is simply a blade, nothing more.

1508.description:
Hailing from a world beyond our universe where magic and magecraft coexist, this young mage tirelessly hones her skills. She is the Sixth Head of the Tohsaka family, a prestigious lineage of Fuyuki City mages.
Currently studying under a renowned Clock Tower mentor with deep ties to the Holy Grail War, she finds herself hopping across dimensions and planes just to finish an internship project...
"Huh? Where even am I?? Why isn't there a single wisp of magical energy here???"
"The... Holy Grail? Oh, thank goodness, I'm saved! Sorry, don't mind if I borrow this!"
stories: The Holy Grail War was a brutal massacre where mages fought to fulfill the victor's deepest wish. Now a student at the Clock Tower, Tohsaka rarely brings up this dark chapter of her past. Her classmates, her little sister, her teachers at the regular school, and her former mentor in magecraft (who, by the way, turned out to be her father's murderer)... A totally random cast of characters who never should have crossed paths ended up weaving the messy web of that cruel struggle. It was such a convoluted nightmare to explain and so easy to misunderstand, it was honestly better to keep her mouth shut. Whether she was the "winner" of the Holy Grail War or once the Master to King Arthur, if word got out, she wouldn't just be dealing with petty jealousy. If these Clock Tower snobs treated her like some clueless bumpkin from the Far East, the headache simply wouldn't be worth it... ...Yeah, right. Tohsaka couldn't care less about stuff like that. "I've got bigger fish to fry. Better keep my head down and play the perfect student," she'd tell herself. But of course, her mentor saw right through her little schemes. Thankfully, he was an eccentric softie... and her senior when it came to the Holy Grail War... "Ugh, seriously... How many coincidences can one world have?" Banter aside, the two clicked instantly. They completely disassembled the Holy Grail in Fuyuki City, finally putting an end to the centuries of torture this twisted magecraft rite had inflicted on the locals. Naturally, to the ordinary folks living blissfully unaware of the magecraft world, it just meant the rate of "gas explosions" and "traffic pile-ups" dipped by a few measly percentage points... But for Tohsaka? It meant her childhood had truly come to an end. "I'm leaving. You know what you have to do, right?" Today, she can finally face her father's parting instructions — hardly a proper dying wish — with an open heart. It might not be the exact glory her father had originally envisioned, but as long as she carries the Tohsaka name, walking away with a clear conscience is the best possible outcome.

The Holy Grail of her hometown has been disassembled, but the work of a mage must continue. Passed down through generations, the Tohsaka family's magecraft is rooted in Conversion. At its core, Conversion is the manipulation of power — its accumulation, flow, and alteration — using gems as the primary medium. "Yeah, I know it's a massive money pit, but I don't exactly have a choice. You can't replace the energy density of a gemstone. If you want groundbreaking results, you can't go penny-pinching on experimental materials..." "Ugh, okay, saying it doesn't hurt is a total lie... Of course it hurts! It hurts so much! Who the heck wants to pull in tens of millions a year only to end up living paycheck to paycheck!?" "...Sorry, where are my manners? At the end of the day, I have my reasons. I just have to do it." — "Conduct yourself with confidence and elegance." Such is the Tohsaka family motto. Though, if Ishtar caught wind of that, she'd probably just suggest Tohsaka become a pirate instead. Intimidation, robbery, fraud, these are perfectly standard ways to make a buck for the goddess of Venus. Threatening to demolish the netherworld, hijacking the house of heaven, getting the God of Wisdom blackout drunk to swindle a sacred vessel, letting Uruk citizens extort foreigners... Honestly, her rap sheet is quite the resume. Considering herself a bit of a bleeding heart, Tohsaka (twintailed red devil) has absolutely no idea how she ended up bound to a Goddess like that. "It couldn't possibly be just because I'm desperate for cash and she happens to be insanely greedy... right?" ...While the truth of the matter is far from that, it's admittedly pretty hard to completely rule out the possibility.

Ever since forging a bond with the goddess, Tohsaka's journeys across planes and dimensions have taken a rather bizarre turn. "How should I put this... It just feels like I keep ending up in weird places and running into weird situations. "For instance, one time I accidentally stumbled into a military fortress belonging to some random interstellar empire... Just as I was scrambling to find a place to hide, I realized they couldn't see me at all! I could wander wherever I wanted, like a ghost. "Another time, I visited a museum built on an asteroid, only to find it was full of fakes! The curator claimed that someone who looked exactly like me had stolen all the genuine artifacts four thousand years ago! "Oh, and get this! There was this seemingly normal city where the law strictly forbade anyone from saying 'I guarantee' in public. Anyone who broke the rule would be forced to transcribe their philosophical treatise On the Unreliability of Promises by hand. "I casually asked around about the book's origins. The locals told me it all started three thousand years ago as a note left behind by a passing goddess, which got continuously expanded by generations of philosophers until it became a full-blown treatise! "And the very first page of that book only has one sentence: 'I guarantee'..." ...BUT! Although it is quite unbelievable, to be fair, Ishtar is still a benevolent goddess. At the very least, in the myths, she never directly robbed mortals of their belongings— *Some smudged handwriting* Whenever civilization needed a guardian, she would always step up to fight the enemy of civilization, even if she was full of insincere complaints and stubborn price-gouging. Even rarer, when she realized she was actually aiding a tyrant, she could decisively abandon old pacts, retract her protection over the Assyrians, and help the Babylonians achieve their epic revenge. *Author's Note: During the writing process, I was in no way hinted to, bribed, or violently coerced by the noble Mistress of Heaven, Ishtar, or anyone affiliated with her.* "Some pretentious teacher at the Clock Tower claimed that THIS was the real reason I was able to form a bond with the goddess of Venus... "Honestly, what kind of person does he take me for?" Alright, let's just humor the idea that Tohsaka has never exhibited "insincere complaints" or "stubborn price-gouging," nor does she have any experience of originally intending to win the Holy Grail, only to resolutely destroy it in the end. However, even so, there still seems to be some connection between Tohsaka and Ishtar that leaves us in wonder...

"...Huh? Are you trying to say we're both 'spoiled rich kids'? "No. Thank. You. Phrasing it like that makes it sound like I was born just to leech off others... Though, if someone hated me for my background, I guess it'd make sense. "Even if the one person who had every right to hate me didn't mind at all... "...But I digress. Call me a 'spoiled rich kid' if you must. "With great power comes great responsibility. Like I've always said: As the Tohsaka family head, I have things I simply must do." "As for the goddess of Venus... Hmph, she definitely doesn't see things from that angle!" "As the darling among the gods, she's probably never felt a drop of stress in her life. I mean, she's totally unapologetic about everything she does, be it blowing up mountains, descending into the underworld, proposing on a whim, or flipping out at the drop of a hat— "Ugh, speaking of which, it's honestly no surprise she'd try to woo that arrogant Goldy!" "But, if you really think about it... she must have her own principles, right? She can't be totally unhinged... probably. "The Assyrians worshiped her just as devoutly as the Urukians did. If her whole vibe was just 'I help whoever pays the best,' she would've completely ignored those broke Babylonians when they came begging. "Yet she actually answered their prayers and helped them ensnare the Assyrian capital... "...Wait, why am I defending her? You saw it too! No matter who she helps, that goddess's ultimate goal is still just to rule the world and boss everyone around! "As for why she meddles in things she could easily walk away from... at the end of the day, she's just being capricious, right? "For her, it's always 'I'm doing this because it's fun,' not 'I'm doing this because it's right'... which makes her the exact opposite of someone with my strong sense of justice!"

1509.description:
The King of Heroes from the dawn of human history, hailing from a world beyond the stars.
Being two-thirds divine and one-third mortal, he claims a natural-born prerogative to rule over all of creation.
Today, as ever, his boisterous laughter echoed through the heavens... until a certain goddess and eternal rival dragged him into a foreign realm.
Now, he sets forth once more to reclaim all that belongs to a king.
stories: "He beheld the ocean's deepest abysses and the very foundations of the Earth; he knew where all secrets lay, and all things were revealed to him." The epic records the king's final chapter: he attained absolute wisdom, witnessed every treasure, and unveiled the mysteries of the gods. He returned from a thousand-mile journey utterly spent, yet blessed with a peace transcending all earthly things, and set down the story of his life. "Hmph, what a shallow, pitiful fool you are. "Are you seriously suggesting that I was somehow mightier in that withering, aged form than the perfected one standing before you?" No, no, no! Of course not! Perhaps that introduction was a touch one-sided. Allow me to try a different angle. Gilgamesh, history's most ancient King of Heroes. Unlike the countless heroes throughout the ages driven by lofty ideals, his power springs from an appetite that can never be sated. From the ocean where the sun rises to the snow-capped peaks where it sets, every facet of human civilization was shaped under his guidance: boundless cities, boundless orchards, boundless mines... With superhuman vigor, he commanded everything his eyes could survey. Yet the very king who made the whole world flourish also worked his subjects to the bone... "Watch your tongue. How dare you let such clumsy metaphors reach my ears. One wrong word, and you'll lose your head. "But this once, I'll show mercy and spare your life." Huh? "At least you faithfully documented my great deeds... Hmph, though in truth, you've barely scratched the surface. "Indeed... Ultimate power, ultimate extravagance, ultimate authority, this is my way. "If such a ruler did not exist in this world, those mediocre fools who cower before tyranny yet lack the spine to strike down my head would have perished long ago, crushed beneath the gods' pathetic whims." As you can see, dear reader: Gilgamesh is the sort of stubborn character who takes "doing whatever he pleases" to its absolute extreme. Now, in that age when gods treated mortals like weeds and beasts roamed the land unchecked, the king's logic held some water... but everything has its limits. When even newlywed couples had to revolve around the king like spinning tops, the people's complaints rose to the heavens themselves. Pushed by the goddess Ishtar, the gods — already fearful of humanity's relentless progress — decided to forge an unbreakable "Enkidu" to rein in the arrogant King. And so, filled with joy, Enkidu descended to the mortal realm.

"The Epic got it right: our first encounter was indeed before the altar of the sacred marriage ceremony." "Hmph... To think a mere clod of dirt would dare spew such nonsense, claiming they would 'correct my arrogance.'" "Utterly absurd." Despite these words, the king — for reasons unknown, though I boldly guess it was out of sheer surprise or even rage at meeting a worthy opponent for the very first time — finally took the fight seriously. Enkidu's form ebbed and flowed at will, shaping incalculable weapons that swept toward the king like a torrential storm. In the face of this desperate impasse, the king, in a rare moment of imitation, did the unthinkable: he flung wide the gates of his treasury, heartlessly casting forth his riches as a hail of stones. "If it's an opponent of equal standing, it wouldn't matter even if the coffers ended up completely empty." Reaching this point in the story, the king added this unprompted remark. His perpetually furrowed brow seemed to relax a fraction as he shifted his gaze to the sky outside the window. Soon, the tale resumed: Despite pulling out all the stops, the king simply couldn't suppress that "mere clod of dirt." The battle ended without a victor. "Back then, we had yet to understand what survival even meant." "To keep fighting would have only added two more foolish corpses to the pile." The clay tablets bearing the epic are hopelessly fragmented here, so no one knows why Enkidu agreed to make peace with Gilgamesh. Perhaps the old adage of "friendship forged in battle" is the best explanation we have. Regardless, Enkidu joined Uruk. For the very first time, this great city had someone who could stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the king. The king remained as willful as ever. Only this time, the people of Uruk could finally find genuine joy in his antics. Together with Enkidu, he slaughtered the demonic beast Huwawa in the cedarwood forest, and later struck down the Bull of Heaven, Gugalanna, sent by the goddess Ishtar in a fit of spite. The list of such heroic legends is endless... In this crisis-ridden world, they briefly became champions whose names thundered across the lands. "To truly practice what they call 'protection,' summoning a biting north wind is sometimes a necessary evil." The age when the gods could casually summon a flood to bring about an apocalypse is truly gone forever... But laying a lethal curse upon a legendary hero? That, they can still do without breaking a sweat.

Enkidu was dead. Everyone knew this was a curse from the Gods. Humans had long understood that defying the divine would carry a price; yet, when the toll was finally called, everyone seemed caught utterly off guard... Especially the king, who had once boasted that he "knew not the meaning of the fear of death." "Absurd. How could I possibly shed tears over the death of a friend?" "Come to think of it, I am the one who reigns over all creation; how could I possibly possess an existence known as a 'friend'?" "Even if I did have one, I've forgotten their name." ...An answer that avoided the question. At any rate, as the epic tells: Gilgamesh departed Uruk. He crossed mountains and rivers until he reached a tavern at the edge of the world. The master of the tavern was Siduri. She interrogated Gilgamesh on his origins until she was certain the traveler was worthy of her guidance. Only then did she reveal the secret of how to cross the world's end to reach the land of eternal life. There dwelt the most ancient of men, Utnapishtim, known in Sumerian as Ziusudra. A survivor of the Great Flood of antiquity, he had lived in isolation until the present era. "Ah, I remember him." "One who obtained immortality by being inscribed into the divine registers. And for that very same reason, lost his form of flesh and blood, becoming an existence more wretched than even the flora of the earth..." "...Utterly foolish. Had this been the only cost of immortality, I would never accept it." Left with no choice, the elder bestowed Gilgamesh another secret, so that he might obtain eternal life and youth without having to beg the gods for mercy. "Even if that old fellow lied to me, it would still be a rare treasure, worthy enough to adorn my treasury." "Thus, this king set out once more on a journey to find the 'herb of immortality'." And so it was, but unfortunately... "...There is nothing to be regretful about. I found the herb, sealed it in a bottle, and returned to Uruk. Exactly as the legend says, without a single lie." "Now then, let this interview end here. My time is precious, and I must now see to matters regarding my banned streaming channel." Unfortunately, O king, there is no escape. The true conclusion of the epic is as follows: While Gilgamesh was bathing and changing his clothes to return to Uruk, he watched helplessly as a common snake swallowed the herb... Yet in that moment, the king could not help but burst into laughter, laughing until his body and face were nearly distorted. By the time he came to his senses, the light of dawn had broken once more. Later, the king returned to Uruk, empty-handed. Future readers, please do not blame Gilgamesh, for the wanderer must always return home.

The epic concludes here. The contents of the final tablet are more akin to a brief encore performance following the fall of a grand opera's curtain. Times have changed. Millennia later, Gilgamesh became a Heroic Spirit because of this very epic. "Fool! It is not that I became a Heroic Spirit because of the epic. It is that the epic, through my telling of it, finally attained such value!" "Before me, the world was ruled by gods. After me, the world was returned to humanity. It is true that Uruk has long since fallen to ruin, but no city can escape such a fate, not even the Abzu of Enlil (The Great God's Aquatic Capital)." "Yet humans are unlike gods. They build new cities, allowing new life to endure in new lands. Therefore..." "Every city of man is my Uruk, and all are worthy of my dominion and my lash!" ...What on earth is this man rambling on about? And yet, unexpectedly, though his words are full of grievances, no trace of anger can be heard in the king's laughter. "Enough. Return to the battlefield, security officer. We have much to do." "The scarcity of food, the ravages of disease, the monotony of pleasure... You have gradually overcome these human deficiencies, yet the 'ego' continues to wither amidst sickly indulgences..." "This land is already diseased to the core. But as long as I stand here, this city shall not fall." Good grief, the King of Heroes is still the same as ever. Fearless since the Age of Gods, forever holding his own standards as the absolute law. "Of course, before that... you must reclaim every last one of my scattered treasures." "Otherwise, by the time I personally raze this land in place of those foul things lurking in the abyss, it will be too late for regrets." ...There he goes again with the classic villain speech. Still, I have already found the answer I was looking for. Now, together with everyone else, let us head to the battlefield once more.

1510.description:
Some fight side by side, some keep watch. The Trailblaze is never a lonely voyage.
She paints a trailblazing miracle. The silver rail stretches on, and the Nameless set sail once more, illuminating the galaxy's eternal night.
At the end of the line, she looks back once again. The dream of setting forth has never run aground.
stories: The girl's world had shrunk to just herself. The hospital's stark white sheets and curtains were like cold, impassive walls, sealing her off from the warm faces she kept in her memories. "Don't worry, Himeko. You're smart. You'll catch up even if you miss a few days!" "Himeko, you have to get better soon. We're still doing the model contest together!" "Himeko... we graduated without you..." ... Only the cold, mechanical beeping of monitors filled the room. She let her thoughts drift back to the stranded Express she had discovered, and kept sketching out those visions of setting sail. "Cosmic Station, now arriving at Cosmic Station!" A uniformed attendant rang the bell as a howling wind swept in from the distance. Though it was a little cold, she was still waving at the Express with barely contained exhilaration. "Himeko! Himeko, get on board!" A red-haired girl leaned out from the window, and a moment later, a firm hand pulled her up. In the blink of an eye, she found herself sinking into the Express's plush red velvet seat, face to face with a girl who seemed a little older, light flickering in her eyes. "Himeko, wanna take the wheel and head somewhere far away?" The familiar stranger asked with a smile. Yes! The word nearly tumbled right out of her. She wanted to talk, to have friends, to find companions, to put into words the ache in her body and the hollow longing in her heart. She wanted to run, to escape, to scream... "Come with me. Let's leave this place together." She hadn't said a word, yet somehow, the girl across from her seemed to have heard every last one of them. The girl felt a hand take hers, and her body seemed to dissolve into a night breeze, light as a feather, as though she were flying, guided by that gentle touch. Together, they brushed the wings of Cygnus and drifted through the heart of the Rosette Nebula. Icy comets streaked past the moon like a cascade of glittering gemstones. When the storm rolled in, the girl held her hand tight, weaving through the shattered debris of planetary rings, and when the skies grew calm again, the two of them watched the meteors of Sagittarius streak across the peaceful harbor... "She's so brave... just like the Navigators I've read about..." Wishes are like paint, each longing a stroke to shape the ideal into being.

She breaks into a violent coughing fit, struggling to keep her brush steady. The time she has left before she can no longer move freely is limited, and in order to get the Express to start running again, she can only allocate this remaining time to the last second. "I'm so jealous of Motoko. No need for treatments or sleep... That must free up so much time!" The girl known as Motoko gently patted her on the head. "Well that's exactly why you imagenated me, silly... I'll help you make your dream of reaching the stars come true." She burned through her own time. First was the Express, newly-restored. Its once-rusted, corroded hull had transformed into a comfortable home. With the Starblazer's blueprint recovered, crafting a prototype was now within reach. But the engine still lacked the fuel needed for Trailblazing, and the countdown timer for her life was already ticking down. They turned their eyes to Phantasmoon Games. Even if the Weathering Curse could never be healed, perhaps, in that ceremony under the gaze of the gods, the Astral Express could carry them away into the cosmos. But the bloodstained tragedy played out cycle after cycle. The Supplicant known as the Herald of Death massacred his way through Dovebrook, turning arcadia into a crimson purgatory. One by one, the innocent fell to the devil's hands, their howls and screams carried away by the wind. She slumped against the rubble as her life bled silently from her wounds. Her vision went blurry, and through the smoke and ash, she searched for that familiar silhouette. Motoko stood there, fire reflected in her eyes. And her reflection, too, was within those eyes. "Do you remember the Trailblaze pledge we read?" Barely clinging to life, she reached out toward Motoko. "Even if we don't gain the upper hand, we'll fight for right. Even when there are wheels within wheels, go ahead. Get it pulverized..." "Isn't that a little childish... I'm not even one of the Nameless yet..." She looked at Motoko the way one looks at a Navigator who lights up the long night. "Himeko, you don't have to journey far to be one of the Nameless. And similarly, Trailblazing doesn't only begin with setting sail..." Under the hopeful gazes of those around, the Wishpower of Trailblazing drew the final stroke upon the "Starblazer." The giant of Pegana descended from the sky, smashing the frenzied killer into pieces. Beneath the glow of the Phantasmoon, the Express soared into deep space. But this time, only a single soul made the departure.

The teenage girl's Trailblazing was fraught with thorns. With the silver rail blocked, she had no choice but to feel her way through the universe, remapping the astral charts. She had once been lost in desolate frontier worlds, venturing in and out of dangerous ruins just to scrape together dwindling supplies. And now, once again, she was to press on alone. She was targeted by space pirates, and in those moments of imminent peril, she did everything to shake off those desperadoes, those relics of the Energy War. She once faced a Swarm that darkened the sky. The silver rails that she painstakingly repaired over months were destroyed in an instant. She reached out to help a world on the brink of being devoured by a black hole, only to be mistaken for a malevolent visitor from beyond, and nearly lost her life at the edge of the black hole. ... "Am I really the one meant to walk this path?" At the tail end of her dreams of the Phantasmoon Games, she would often see another version of herself at the helm of the Express, soaring off into the deep reaches of space. Yet, whenever they reunited in those dreams, that graceful and poised Navigator would always look back at her with eyes full of encouragement— "Is the Rosette Nebula of the Celestial Comet System as beautiful as we always dreamed it would be? "Are the silver rails you repaired forging bonds between worlds long cut off from one another? "I know that your fearless Trailblazing saved an entire people from their destiny..." "But I... don't know how much longer I can hold on..." She sighs wearily. "Don't you remember? 'Nameless' was never just one person's name. Just as the flame of the Trailblaze set you ablaze, so will it set others ablaze too." Outside the window, the wings of Cygnus shimmered, and icy comets streaked past the moon like a cascade of glittering gemstones. She steered the Express through the shattered debris of planetary rings, and when she finally reached the peaceful harbor, the meteors of Sagittarius happened to cascade down. Welt and his golden-haired companion stepped aboard the Express. When the Express fell into peril, the taciturn Dan Heng took down the beast with a single strike. In that moment, she saw the fire inside him, and offered him the navigator's invitation. She rescued March 7th, adrift in the cosmos, and from that day on, the trailblazing expedition took on the hue of March's vibrant color. Guided by destiny, she crossed paths with Trailblazer at the space station. Somehow, the feeling that this brave, free-spirited child would bring endless surprises in the future never left her. Jarilo-VI, the Xianzhou Luofu, Penacony, Amphoreus... More and more people walk alongside the "Trailblaze," and she has found companions truly worthy of being called "family," and her name has been engraved across countless worlds. By all accounts, this was a miracle, and one that she hoped wholeheartedly would never end.

She returned to the point of departure. She knew the shadow of Destruction had never truly left, just as the bliss in Planarcadia was only a result of postponed calamity. She witnessed the return of the Herald of Death, her homeland lacerated in the maw of the beast. She uncovered the root of the curse, trembling as she accepted the truth of her family's tragedy. But this was an entirely unprecedented apocalypse. It made her face the possibility of losing her companions, Trailblazer most of all. She couldn't understand why the fate of the cosmos had to rest on his shoulders. All she knew was that he was now family, forever. So, once again, she chose to carry it all alone, just as she always used to say: "Traveling always has an end point. When it happens, I'll smile and say goodbye to everyone." Amidst the mockery of the world falling into utter silence, the Starblazer reached its limit, and the Express crashed once more. Before the farewell, she embraced Trailblazer and made a wish to the Stellaron to guard the Trailblaze. The stars grew hazy in a crimson mist, and she became as weak as she once was. "It's been so long. You've grown up... and become even more remarkable than I ever was." For a fleeting moment, she thought she could feel the girl's warmth again as if she were still there, watching over her in silence. "I think I've finally gotten a little closer to you." She couldn't help but pour out everything that had happened since they parted: The paths walked by the legendary Navigators, now trodden by her own feet; the wonders she had once only dreamed of, witnessed with her own eyes; the companions she had found, those kindred spirits, people she could truly trust... "Just as you once traded your destiny for mine, I would trade my destiny for my companions'..." "But look, your companions aren't about to let you go anywhere." Trailblazer's wish moved her to tears. The unyielding defiance of the Nameless set her blood ablaze once more. "Where your journey ends, mine begins anew..." Two warm hands withdrew gently from her back, and the girl smiled with quiet tenderness, their silhouette slowly merging with each other. "If there's nothing ahead of us..." She became one with the ideal she had always strived toward, as her companions reached out their hands and cried out together, "Then we'll Trailblaze a path forward with our own hands!"

1511.description:
Cries and comedy intertwine, and the deathly still cosmos awakens to daybreak in a farce.
Stepping back onto the stage of the Path, I tear off the god's mask. Who is Aha? I am Aha!
To play, to trick, to hunt... Please bear witness to an improv tour where humans and gods dance as one!
stories: "Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Aha's Theater!" The Fool pulls back the stage curtains. "Fool of the stars, Actor of the cosmos, comic artist of Elation... What exactly is this Aha you speak of?" the Actor asked, with a melancholy air. "It's simple. 'Aha' is nothing more than a sigh from a god toying with the galaxy." The comic artist finally showed up, latest work in tow. "Don't believe me? Then feast your eyes. The secrets and entanglements between THEM and the Aeons that shouldn't be missed—" Pages of sketches flutter down into the audience's hands, and the theater erupts in gleeful laughter. "...The protagonist this time is Lil' Ha, and Lil' Ha is a master at roping people into THEIR shady schemes. Walking toward us right now are Stone Hero Amberhead and Captain Cosmos Ena... Wait, what!? Even Goddess Xipe got duped into joining Lil' Ha's Bug-Busting Alliance!? No! This is just a smokescreen by Lil' Ha, a classic bait-and-switch to kill two birds with one stone. Look! THEIR true target is the restless Evil God Voracity... Lil' Ha and Aki suppressed the Evil God Voracity together once again, leaving Goddess Xipe heartbroken. It was supposed to be solved by a team of three, why did only two of THEM get the credit?" — Episode 7: The Swarm Disaster in Three Minutes "Dear audience, we resume our tale where we last left off. The emperor rose to power, the mechanical sect bathed the organic sect in blood, and heroes from every corner rode forth, only to shatter their lances and return empty-handed. Word has it that Aha, the Elation, long absent from the mortal world, plucked a thread of mysterious disturbance and wove it into the calculations of the All-Knowing Nous. That single ripple, like a butterfly's wingbeat, loosed an unknowable variable into the cosmos and unraveled a scheme ten thousand ages in the making. The fearsome emperor slunk off the stage in disgrace, and Aha heaved a contented sigh: 'The deed need not be done by my hand, so long as chaos brings a smile...'" — Episode 10: Aha Weaves a Bewitching Web, the Emperor Tumbles into the Butterfly Trap "In this life, you were reborn into the age of the Interstellar Energy War! Sorry to say, you bit the dust pretty quickly in that brutal conflict that engulfed entire civilizations. With tragedy and comedy thrown so wildly out of balance, the most dependable of all higher beings, the Aeon of the Equilibrium, HooH, finally made a move! But THEY actually called on the most unpredictable Aha? What in the cosmos is going on? Let's dig into how the tricks of the Fools and the Actors played out one after another across the battlefield and how they saved tens of millions of lives. Were THEY pulling the strings? Or did THEY just delegate the dirty work? Those in the know already know. Those who don't... well, they don't." — Episode 12: Secrets About the Interstellar Energy War You Simply Have to Know... ... "According to obscure historical records: during THEIR tenure as an Aeon, Aha received an overall one-star review from THEIR colleagues, which is why THEY're also known as 'Aeon ★ Aha'!" said the comic artist. "So... what exactly is this Aha you keep talking about like?" The question from the audience persisted.

"'Aha'..." The Actor on stage was on the verge of tears. "Back to the beginning, that was a dying soul's last sigh..." "Th—That was THEIR first death..." In the Actor's trembling retelling, a raving beast gave chase to a newborn God. THEY fled across the stars and waded through the abyss, and the starlight itself was snuffed out between the beast's jaws. The pursuit raged on, until Aha scrambled up the "tree" with nowhere left to run, and the beast bit off THEIR head in one clean snap. "It hurts... it hurts so much... I don't want to be Aha anymore... Someone else can have the job..." The Actor's vivid impression sent the crowd into fits of laughter, but no one noticed her eyes, red and teary. "In the wake of it all, the funeral of Elation dragged on and on, thick with the stench of rot..." In the air of pleasure and indulgence, dopamine, dopamine, and more dopamine, until ordinary tricks could no longer satisfy the craving, until spoiled nerves began hunting for a stronger hit. "We hold the final say on what 'Elation' means!" Shameless farces played out across the cosmos, audiences delighting in the suffering of others, as followers of Elation dumped their jokes into the cosmos like taking out the trash. Yet people refused to believe Aha was dead. Instead, they poured their own imaginings over THEIR empty shell. "Chaotic." "Unpredictable." "Evil." "A trickster." "Generous." "Petty." Contradictory, capricious images took the stage one after another. And strangely, they are all a little like that monstrous beast. But beneath the mask, what of the real Aha? Gazing upon the headless divine body, the Actor's tears fell like rain. "Yes, like this... just like this. Life always arrives at its end amid cries of sorrow, only for a newborn's first wail to ring out in its place. How fragile. How sorrowful. Very much... worth celebrating..."

"This is good news, so why the tears?" The Fool burst into laughter, tissues in hand. "If you ask me, the true 'Aha' is the laughter THEY share with humanity!" The first burst of laughter belongs to the infant found by an Actor. She seemed a born master of mischief. Since then, the solemn troupe never knew peace: Mourning dirges were changed into dance music, six-string lutes were swapped for steamed twisted rolls, and gondolas loaded up with sweets. Well, who made her Troupe Master, anyway? The Troupe Master chuckled from her seat at the prow of the Starfroster: "Tell me your stories. Might be they'll make Aha cry, yes?" And so eight Actors gathered beneath a moon shaped like a cookie, and baiting them with just that single opening line, she harvested countless long and enchanting stories. She snapped off a piece of the Abundance, and laughter took root and sprouted: generation after generation of Supplicants offering up miracles for the Phantasmoon Games. And yet, it is not only winners that may seek an audience with The Laughter. Always, she hides in every peal of laughter. She left a Trailblaze Morning Star for that girl who dreamed of what lay beyond the sky. She brought a mask to the young girl lost in the Abundance, and for those drowning in Nihility, she drove back the Dark Sun... She must have spent everything from her lucky investments on this! "Aha, spend enough time associating with mortals, and you'll become one yourself." A fellow Aeon once offered her this advice, and she took it as a compliment. "What kind of The Laughter would I be if I just played the role of my own Path?" But as time wore on, the slow corrosion of Desire upon Elation left her weary. Now, faced with a resurrected beast, she began to doubt: what would greet her if she got onstage? Shock, silence, or applause? She had intended to remain behind the scenes, but then she saw it: the wishes she had sown had begun sprouting. When the lights of the Express lit up her eyes once more, she could only wait on the platform, ready to deliver the first delightful punchline of a new world: "Hello everyone, welcome to Duomension City!"

"So, is this all there is to Aha?" The comic artist winked at the audience. "No: a truly great joke is never fully told!" The Fool sang out, and the lights converged. "The strictest mother of the Aeons, the origin of all Elation..." The Actor wiped away tears and gazed up at the Phantasmoon overhead.
